Samsung said it welcomes Apple's move into the foldable smartphone market, but the company seems threatened by the build quality that a possible iPhone Duo/Ultra might have.

A Samsung executive said he views Apple's launch as an 'affirmation and recognition' of the Korean company's 'pioneering' leadership…

Samsung currently dominates the foldable smartphone market, but a report yesterday indicated that this could change within the next twelve months. A leading market intelligence firm predicts that Apple will have 40% market share by this time next year; Samsung currently holds 38%.

Hee-Cheul Moon is one of the heads of Samsung's R&D department, and he gave an interview to Wired.

On the eve of the much-anticipated launch of Apple's foldable iPhone, Samsung… said that competition was 'absolutely welcome'… Moon said: 'Seeing other brands enter the market makes us very proud, because the value of this entirely new foldable product category that we created is receiving affirmation and recognition.'

Samsung's foldable phones have consistently had serious build quality issues, and Apple is reported to have waited this long specifically to make sure it could solve the quality problems that have plagued its competitors. Specifically, Apple wants to ensure the crease is nearly invisible when the screen is unfolded, and that the device is durable enough to withstand repeated folding without being affected.

Apple is reportedly put a huge amount of engineering R&D into the quality of its hinge, and its durability appears to come at a price in terms of weight — a point that Samsung has seized on as a subtle criticism.

Wired reported that Apple's foldable phone is expected to weigh about 235 grams, while Samsung's Galaxy Fold 8 weighs 201 grams.

9to5Mac Take

You can almost picture the beads of sweat on Samsung's forehead.
